business_model.claim: The company designs, builds, markets and sells single-family detached homes, attached townhomes and condominiums, urban infill and active lifestyle homes in planned residential developments.
quotes: Through its subsidiaries, HEI designs, constructs, markets, and sells single-family detached homes, attached townhomes and condominiums, urban infill, and active lifestyle homes in planned residential developments and is one of the nation’s largest builders of residential homes.

business_model.claim: Its buyers are individual homebuyers across price tiers. Base prices range from $182,000 to $1,191,000, and the fiscal 2025 average sales price including options was $519,000.
quotes: We market and build homes for first-time buyers, move-up buyers, luxury buyers, active lifestyle buyers and empty nesters.

business_model.claim: The company has two operations, homebuilding and financial services. Homebuilding is reported in three segments: Northeast, Southeast and West.
quotes: Our homebuilding operations consist of three reportable segments: Northeast, Southeast and West.

business_model.claim: Financial services provides mortgage loans and title services to the company's own homebuyers.
quotes: Our financial services operations provide mortgage loans and title services to the customers of our homebuilding operations.

business_model.basis: stated in the 10-K Item 1, as of the fiscal 2025 filing
business_model.claim: Excluding unconsolidated joint ventures, the company was offering homes in 140 communities in 27 markets in 13 states.
quotes: Excluding unconsolidated joint ventures, we are currently offering homes for sale in 140 communities in 27 markets in 13 states throughout the United States.

business_model.claim: Home sales make up most of revenue. In the quarter ended July 31, 2026, sale of homes was 679,042, land sales and other was 3,032 and financial services was 23,672, out of total revenues of 705,746 (table in thousands).
Home sale revenue moves with deliveries and average price. Q3 fiscal 2026 deliveries fell to 1,259 from 1,431, and average sales price rose to $539,350 from $537,421.
quotes: The decreases were primarily due to a 12.0% decline in home deliveries for both the three and nine month periods of 2026, partially offset by increases in average sales price of 0.4% and 2.3%, respectively.

business_model.basis: stated in the 10-K MD&A and 10-Q MD&A tables
business_model.claim: Land sales are ancillary to homebuilding and can be lumpy. Nine-month land sales were $68,224 in fiscal 2026 against $20,623 a year earlier (table in thousands).
quotes: Land sales are ancillary to our homebuilding operations and are expected to continue in the future but may fluctuate significantly.

business_model.claim: Mortgage rates and the availability of mortgage financing drive demand, because most buyers need a mortgage.
quotes: Because the large majority of our customers require mortgage financing, increases in interest rates or the decreased availability of mortgage financing could considerably impair the affordability of our homes, lower demand for our products, limit our marketing effectiveness and limit our ability to fully realize our backlog.

business_model.basis: stated in the 10-Q MD&A, with the counterpoint from the 8-K release
business_model.claim: Incentives and mortgage rate buydowns are the main recent drag on margin. Q3 fiscal 2026 homebuilding gross margin before interest and land charges fell to 14.6% from 17.3%.
quotes: The decreases were primarily due to increased use of incentives and concessions, including additional mortgage interest rate buydowns, to improve affordability.

business_model.claim: The company deliberately prioritizes sales pace over gross margin.
quotes: In the current homebuilding environment, we remain focused on driving financial performance by increasing sales pace rather than achieving a higher gross margin.

business_model.basis: stated in the 10-K MD&A cost of sales table
business_model.claim: The largest cost of a home is housing, land and development, at 71.3% of fiscal 2025 home sales. Financing concessions rose to 3.9% from 2.5%.
Quick-move-in (QMI) homes are a sales tool because they make mortgage rate buydowns affordable for the company to offer.
quotes: QMI homes also allow us to offer customers mortgage rate buydowns that would be cost prohibitive on homes with a longer time until delivery.

business_model.claim: The sales mix has shifted slightly toward to-be-built contracts, which generally carry higher gross margins than QMI homes.
quotes: Although we remain focused on the sale of QMI homes, there has been a subtle shift toward more to-be-built home contracts, which in general have higher gross margins than QMI homes.

business_model.claim: Land is mainly controlled through options to limit cash at risk. Walking away from options creates write-off charges: 14,902 lots and $18.2 million in fiscal 2025.
quotes: We attempt to acquire land with a minimum cash investment and negotiate takedown options, thereby limiting the financial exposure to the amounts invested in property and predevelopment costs.

business_model.claim: Sale prices are fixed up to 12 months before delivery, which exposes margins to cost inflation.
quotes: We may not be able to recapture increased costs by raising prices in many cases because we fix our prices up to 12 months in advance of delivery when we sign home sales contracts.
